question: [scripted] ECHO-05: does weighing a conclusion again on fresh evidence before committing to it make the fly's stated confidence in its explanations more accurate?
hypothesis: [scripted] A fly that commits to a conclusion at once has a higher Brier score on hidden held-out changes than one that takes a second look first.
competing_hypothesis: [scripted] The evidence that made the first answer likely also makes the second look agree, so it only delays the same answers.
